$comment: MEASURED maximum output length per hosted model, as a boundary PROBE rather than a
configured value. Each row records the largest max_tokens the provider ACCEPTED and
the smallest it REFUSED, so the row is falsifiable: re-run the probe and the two
numbers either still bracket the limit or they do not.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS SEPARATELY FROM players/registry.yaml. C6 in
scripts/qa_coverage_checks.py must decide whether a truncated answer was cut off by
OUR configuration or by the model's own limit. Comparing the registry's ceiling to
the registry's ceiling cannot fail -- a check that derives its reference from the
value being checked is not a check. This file is the independent reference: it comes
from hitting the live endpoint, not from what we chose to send.
A row is EVIDENCE, not a permission. It does not exempt any player from C6; it only
lets C6 tell 'we throttled it' apart from 'the model ran to its own limit'. A record
that does not say what ceiling it sent still fails, whatever this file says.
HOW TO ADD OR REFRESH A ROW. Send one trivial prompt at max_tokens = N against the
real endpoint, bisecting until the HTTP 400 boundary is found:
accepted -> HTTP 200
refused  -> HTTP 400 'too many tokens: max tokens must be less than or equal to X'
Record BOTH numbers, the endpoint, and the date. Never copy a number from a docs page:
measured 2026-09-09, docs.cohere.com/docs/models implied 8000/4000/4000 for these three
models and every one of those was BELOW the true limit. That 96-token shortfall on
command-r-plus published a perfect 1.000 as 0.0.
